scheduled.title: Is Your Student Loan Halal? (You Never Touched What You Owe) #studentloans #islamicfinance
scheduled.description:
You have paid it every month for six years. You have never touched it.

Here is the mechanism nobody explains. You agreed to repay a slice of what you
earn above a threshold — capped, predictable, and it does sound fair. But
interest is charged every day on the WHOLE outstanding balance, and that charge
is uncapped, because it grows with the balance itself.

So there are two flows, not one. Money leaving you, capped. Money joining the
debt, uncapped.

Somewhere between them is a crossover — an income where the two are exactly
equal. Above it, your payment eats the interest and starts on the balance, and
the debt falls. Below it, the balance does not fall slowly. It does not fall at
all. It rises, while you pay it, faithfully, for a decade.

That is not what happens when you default. It is what happens when you comply.

And it cuts the wrong way. The graduate who earns well crosses over, clears the
debt and stops paying. The graduate who earns less pays for thirty years and
clears nothing. Same debt — the one with less money pays longer, and pays more.
Then it is written off, which sounds like mercy. It isn't. The lender's own
forecasts already assume most of that money is never coming back. The write-off
isn't the escape hatch at the end of the machine; it is a line inside the
machine's budget.

Plan Two. Income-driven. Deferment. Same machine.

THE TWO-MINUTE CHECK:

1. Find two published numbers — your interest rate and your repayment threshold.
   Both are on your statement or your servicer's site.
2. Work out a single month. Interest added, against payment taken. If the
   interest is bigger, you are renting the debt, not repaying it.
3. Only then decide about overpaying. Above the crossover it genuinely shortens
   the debt. Far below it, with a write-off coming anyway, it is money burned.
   Same arithmetic, run honestly, in both directions.

Riba is not a tax on borrowing. It is a price charged for time — a number that
grows because the clock moved, not because anything was built, sold or risked.
A debt you service faithfully and cannot reduce is the purest form of it there
is.

You didn't fail to pay it off. You were never paying it off.

The Money Machine, Decoded.

I name no lender, servicer or university. Plan names appear only to make the

current terms. Scholars differ on borrowing under necessity where no
alternative route to education exists. This is financial education, not

Scarce is only half of it. It also has to actually be yours. Most people "holding gold" hold a certificate, an app, or a balance on a screen — a promise that someone else will deliver metal they are holding. That is not gold. That is a claim, and a claim can be diluted.

Gold for gold, hand to hand, same sitting, no delay. Settle now, or it isn't a sale. Physical, allocated, in your possession. No margin, no leverage, no IOU dressed as metal. And metal isn't the only answer — a share of something real that produces works too.

Own the thing, not the claim on the thing.

Part 15 of The Money Machine, Decoded.

_published_scheduled_archive.title: Is Your Pension Halal? (You Never Picked What It Buys) #pension #islamicfinance
_published_scheduled_archive.description:
Your pension owns things you would never buy with your own money. Nobody asked
you — you were opted in, and that included what it buys.

Pension, 401(k), workplace plan: same machine. When you joined you chose a
number — how much goes in. You almost certainly never chose where it goes. That
is the default fund, and most people never move out of it.

What is in it? An index. A basket of the largest listed companies, bought
automatically by size, with no screening at all. That is not a flaw in an index
tracker — it is the definition of one. So the basket holds banks and insurers as
one of its biggest slices, alongside alcohol, gambling, tobacco and weapons.

The banks are the sharp part. A bank's product is not a service, it is interest.
Own the bank and you own the income. That is not a technicality, it is the whole
business.

And here is the part almost nobody knows. Your fund is built to change as you
age — "lifestyling", or a "glide path". It sounds like safety. What it actually
does is sell shares and buy bonds as you approach retirement. A bond is a loan.
You are lending money at interest. The machine moves you deeper into it the
older you get, automatically, as a feature you were never shown.

THE TWO-MINUTE CHECK:

1. Log in and find the name of your fund. If it says "default", "balanced", or a
   retirement year, that is the basket.
2. Search that fund's largest holdings — they are published. You will recognise
   the banks immediately.
3. Open the full fund list and look for a sharia or Islamic option. Most
   workplace schemes have one now, and switching is usually free.

Same contributions. Same employer match. Different basket.

You were opted in by default. Default is still a choice — somebody else just
made it for you.

The Money Machine, Decoded.
